annotations.description: 1.02 checkpoint(s) failed in the last 10 minutes.

diagnosis.summary: Flink checkpoint failures are caused by a Flink taskmanager restart ~2 minutes ago (TaskExecutor shutting down event); the job is back RUNNING/STABLE and completing ~25 checkpoints in the last 5 minutes. The alert window will clear as the 10-minute sliding window moves past the restart-induced failures. All infrastructure appears healthy after a broad disruption ~141 minutes ago that also affected Kafka brokers and ingestion pods.
diagnosis.root_cause: The events-to-iceberg Flink taskmanager (events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2) restarted approximately 1.9 minutes ago (age_minutes=1.9), causing the in-flight checkpoint to fail during the TaskExecutor shutdown. The failed_checkpoints_last_10m metric of 2.104 captures exactly that restart window. The job has since recovered: it is RUNNING/STABLE with 24.995 completed checkpoints in the last 5 minutes (one per 10 seconds as expected). A broader infrastructure event ~140.9 minutes ago (exit_code 255 'Unknown') killed all Kafka brokers, the Flink jobmanager, and both ingestion service pods simultaneously, suggesting a node or cluster disruption; everything recovered but the taskmanager required a second reschedule that triggered this alert. Consumer lag of 650 is expected while the job catches up after restart.
diagnosis.impact: Approximately 2 checkpoints missed during the taskmanager restart, creating a brief window where exactly-once delivery could replay a small amount of data if the job were to fail again. Data visibility in Iceberg is delayed by at most ~20–30 seconds. Consumer lag of 650 events is minor and draining. No data loss expected; end users see at most a brief delay in event materialisation.

evidence.finding: Job is RUNNING/STABLE, uptime_seconds=96 (just restarted), restarts_last_15m=1.018, failed_checkpoints_last_10m=2.104, completed_checkpoints_last_5m=24.995, consumer_lag=650. Taskmanager pod events-to-iceberg-taskmanager-2-2 is only 1.9 minutes old.

Warning JobException on FlinkDeployment/events-to-iceberg 1.9 minutes ago: 'org.apache.flink.util.FlinkExpectedException: The TaskExecutor is shutting down' — directly matches the taskmanager restart timing and the checkpoint failures.

All 5 pods in apps namespace are Running/Ready. Jobmanager, both ingestion pods, and iceberg-exporter all show last_termination reason=Unknown exit_code=255 finished_minutes_ago=140.9, indicating a cluster-wide disruption ~141 min ago.

Kafka cluster Ready, all 3 brokers Running, under_replicated_partitions=0, under_min_isr_partitions=0, offline_partitions=0. All brokers also show last_termination reason=Unknown exit_code=255 finished_minutes_ago=140.9 — same cluster-wide event. Flink consumer lag=650.
All 4 nodes (control-plane + 3 workers across zone-a/b/c) are Ready, no pressure conditions, none unschedulable — cluster infrastructure is healthy now.
Only FlinkCheckpointFailures (1.4 min firing) and an unrelated OpsAgentInvestigationsFailing alert are active. No KafkaBrokerDown or NodeNotReady alerts.
Runbook docs/runbooks/pipeline.md#flinkcheckpointfailures states: 'A single failure during a broker restart or node drain is expected.' Job tolerates 3 consecutive failures before restarting.

proposed_action.rationale: The Flink job is RUNNING/STABLE and already completing checkpoints at the expected 10-second interval (24.995 in the last 5 minutes). The 2 failed checkpoints are consistent with a single taskmanager restart and fall within the runbook's 'expected' category. The job is recovering autonomously; restarting it now would only cause additional checkpoint failures and extend the recovery window. The alert should clear within the next ~8 minutes as the 10-minute window slides past the restart event.

follow_ups: Investigate the root cause of the cluster-wide disruption ~140.9 minutes ago that killed all Kafka brokers, the Flink jobmanager, and both ingestion pods with exit_code 255 'Unknown' — check node/VM events, cloud provider maintenance logs, or kubelet journals for that time window.
Monitor consumer lag (currently 650) over the next 10–15 minutes to confirm it drains to near-zero; if it stays elevated, investigate Kafka throughput or Flink task throughput.
Iceberg-exporter readiness probe failed twice 27.6 minutes ago (connection refused on :9400) — confirm the exporter is now stable and not affecting Iceberg table health metrics.

Consider whether the scheduling of the taskmanager on lakehouse-worker3 (same zone-c node as broker lakehouse-dual-role-1) increases blast radius for future zone disruptions; review pod anti-affinity rules.
The OpsAgentInvestigationsFailing alert has been firing for 54+ minutes — check the ops-agent logs as prior incidents may have gone unnoticed.
